config.title: What Closes in Berlin in Winter - FAQ
config.subtitle: The dates the lakes, outdoor pools, boats and park gates actually change, and what opens in their place.

items.q: What actually closes in Berlin in winter?
items.a: **Less than people expect, and it is almost all outdoors.** The lake bathing season, the neighbourhood outdoor pools and the open-air cinemas end in September. Park and garden gates move to short winter hours from October. Spree boat tours narrow to a weekend winter format from 20 November. What does not change is the part of the city most visitors came for: the museums, the Reichstag dome, the TV Tower, Museum Island and the whole walking centre between Alexanderplatz and Hackescher Markt run all year.

items.q: When do the Berlin lakes and outdoor pools close?
items.a: **Mid-September, in a cluster of a few days.** In 2026 Sommerbad am Insulaner, Sommerbad Humboldthain and Sommerbad Pankow had their last day on 11 September, and Kombibad Gropiusstadt, Sommerbad Neukölln and the Strandbad Wannsee bathing season ended on 13 September. Wannsee then kept a reduced sunbathing and sauna operation until 4 October, from noon on weekdays and from 10:00 at weekends. Exact dates shift by a few days each year, so check the Berliner Bäder-Betriebe calendar before you plan a swim.

items.q: Which Berlin outdoor pool stays open the longest?
items.a: **Sommerbad Kreuzberg, the Prinzenbad, until 30 October.** It is heated, it is directly beside U-Bahn Prinzenstraße on the U1, and it is the only outdoor pool in the city still swimming once the leaves are down. Indoor pools work the other way: the Hallenbäder reopen in waves through September and October, on 7, 14 and 21 September and then 3, 5 and 21 October, so check the specific pool rather than assuming the city is shut.

items.q: Do Spree boat tours run in winter?
items.a: **Yes, but only at the weekend and only for a month.** The regular city tours from Friedrichstraße run through the autumn. Stern und Kreis then switches to the Winterliche Citytour from 20 November to 20 December, Friday to Sunday only. So a November river hour is possible if you put it on a weekend and book it in advance. A Tuesday in December is not.

items.q: What time does it get dark in Berlin in winter?
items.a: **Around 16:00 in December, and everything with a gate closes with it.** Sunset in Berlin is close to 15:55 in the days around the solstice and sunrise is after 08:00, so you get roughly seven and a half hours of daylight. That is why the park gates move: Tempelhofer Feld shuts at 17:00 in December and January, the Botanic Garden exits close at 19:00 from 1 October, and Zoo Berlin stops admitting visitors at 15:30 from 26 October. Plan the outdoor half of the day first and the indoor half after 16:00.

items.q: Is Berlin worth visiting in winter?
items.a: **Yes, and the reason is that the centre has no season.** The Berlin most people come to see is walkable, flat and about three kilometres end to end, and none of it depends on the weather. The saunas in the municipal pools open on 1 November at municipal prices, the Christmas markets start on 23 November, and the Great Tropical Greenhouse in Dahlem is 25 degrees in January. What you lose is the lakes and the long evenings. What you gain is a city with far fewer people in it.
